W2 (empirical), after E047. Tip is E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. Identical-code reruns (E038 0.7525/5.334, E043 0.7497/5.294, E047 0.7544/5.343) show rebuild noise of about 0.3 pp on a 3-seed mean, and about ±0.03 s on time. Population mean is about 0.752, so headroom over the 0.75 bar is about 0.2 pp.

Mechanisms, with the experiments that support them:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch, for 0.0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027). E034 stacked the freeze with +0.5 epoch and saved 0.40 s versus E027 at about 0 pp.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are in the tip. More than 10 time-neutral boosters failed (E025, E029, E030, E032, E044, wd, LS). Averaging, LR shape and wd sit at a flat optimum within about 0.2 pp.
3. Time tracks pixels. Early 20 px for up to about 30% of steps is nearly free (E026, E033). Trimming steps costs about as much as the dial (E040, E041, E031, about 1.5-2.3 s/pp). E045 (smaller early batch) cost +0.2 s for nothing measurable.
4. Backward truncation is the best lever (E028, E034, E036). It is bandwidth-heavy, because frozen blocks skip BN/GELU backward, the update and Lookahead traffic. E037 (60% freeze) cost 0.38 pp. E039 and E042 saved only 0.03-0.05 s. E046 (group-2 freeze for the last 10%) saved 0.24 s with 0.7540 accuracy, which is within noise.
5. Systems overhead outside the step graphs is about 2.5% (E047). It is only reachable with identical math.
6. Noise: 3-seed std is about 0.15-0.2 pp. Any RNG or step-count change reshuffles it. Rebuilds change kernel selection.

Misses: E046 time (predicted 5.27, measured 5.08) and E043 (rebuild noise). I over-predicted time-neutral boosters.

Unsure: whether E046's saving is real and whether it transfers to the PCIe judge. Also unsure whether ReLU gives more than 3% and whether the 0.25 epoch top-up recovers the E046 accuracy.

forecasts.reason: The group-2 freeze saved about 0.24 s in E046 and the top-up costs about 0.1 s, so net time is about 2% below E036. Accuracy sits within noise of the tip.
The reachable overhead is at most about 2%, and some of it probably stays. Math is identical, but rebuild noise dominates the accuracy read.
Elementwise kernels are about 27% of the step. ReLU's cheaper erf-free forward and mask-based backward might save 2-4%. ReLU usually costs a little accuracy against GELU.

cruxes: Is E046's 0.24 s saving real and same-build reproducible, or partly a build artifact?
Does the 0.25-epoch top-up recover about 0.1 pp at about 0.1 s, as the dial predicts?
Does ReLU's activation backward cut memory traffic enough to give more than 3% in time?
